sections.title: Valuation Insights
sections.text: Visa reported consolidated revenue of [[V.fact.revenue]] for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025, reflecting a year‑over‑year increase of [[V.ratio.revenue_growth]] percent. Operating income of [[V.fact.operating_income]] yields an operating margin of [[V.ratio.operating_margin]] percent, indicating efficient cost management. Net income of [[V.fact.net_income]] translates to a return on average equity of [[V.ratio.return_on_average_equity]] percent, highlighting strong profitability relative to shareholders' capital. Total debt, comprising long‑term and current portions of [[V.fact.long_term_debt]] and [[V.fact.current_debt]] respectively, results in a debt‑to‑equity ratio of [[V.ratio.debt_to_equity]], suggesting a moderate leverage profile. Operating cash flow of [[V.fact.operating_cash_flow]] less capex of [[V.fact.capex]] produces free cash flow of [[V.ratio.free_cash_flow]], supporting dividend growth and share buybacks. The price‑earnings multiple based on the dated close of [[V.price]] and diluted EPS of [[V.fact.diluted_eps]] is [[V.ratio.price_earnings]] times, reflecting market valuation relative to earnings. Revenue is defined as consolidated reported revenue, EPS pertains to GAAP diluted earnings per share for Class A common stock, capex captures cash purchases of property, equipment and technology, the fiscal year runs from October 1 to September 30, and the price reflects the unadjusted close on October 27, 2026.

insight.text: Visa generated robust free cash flow, underscoring its ability to fund dividends and share repurchases.
